title: Notifications
intro: nexcrate tells you when something happens, through your own services. Per mailbox you choose what arrives there and how urgent it is.
empty: Nothing set up yet. The plus adds something.

services.ntfy: Push to your phone through ntfy, self-hosted or ntfy.sh. First the instance with address and sign-in, below it the topics you subscribe to in the app.
services.gotify: Push through your own Gotify. Create an application there and enter its token here.
services.telegram: Messages through a Telegram bot of your own. First the bot with its token from @BotFather, below it the chats. Send the bot /start, then nexcrate finds the chat itself.
services.discord: Messages into a Discord channel. In the channel's settings under Integrations, create a webhook and enter its address here. The address is like a password.
services.webhook: A POST with fixed JSON to an address, for Home Assistant, n8n or your own scripts. Not to be confused with the webhooks for programs under System.
services.apprise: On through a self-hosted Apprise API to more than a hundred services, such as Signal, Matrix, Slack or Pushover. Only address and key stand here, the credentials stay in Apprise.
services.email: E-mail through your own mail server. First the server, below it the addresses. The server has to accept the test mail; there is no code here.

fields.name: Name
fields.nameHint: What the tile is called, such as "Phone" or "Family".
fields.urlNtfy: Address of the instance, such as https://ntfy.sh
fields.tokenWebhookHint: Optional, such as "Bearer abc123". Sent as it is as a header.
fields.thread_idHint: Only for groups with topics, else leave it empty.
fields.subject: Subject
fields.subjectHint: Empty: "nexcrate:" and the message's title. {title} puts the title in.
fields.secretKept: Stored. Leave it empty to keep it.

events.health_changed: Something is wrong, or fine again

eventsHint: Per event also how urgent. "Urgent" makes ntfy and Gotify ring through quiet hours, "Quiet" arrives without sound on Telegram.
testSent: The test message is out. Type the code it carries.
mailAccepted: The mail server accepted the test mail. You can save.
chatsNone: Nobody wrote to the bot yet. Send it /start and ask again.
removeText: The tile goes with everything below it. Messages still waiting are not sent any more.
